clinical_utility.what_changes_for_patient: Therapeutic agents (e.g., bevacizumab for tumor, antibiotics for meningitis) remain in CSF longer, improving treatment efficacy while CSF continues to drain. Reduces repeat dosing burden.
clinical_utility.evidence: MODEL_DERIVED — based on V72 moat map analysis (32% half-life reduction model); not validated clinically

scientific_utility.new_capability: Selective molecular retention in CSF — enables localized chemotherapy, antibiotic therapy, and biologic delivery without systemic exposure
scientific_utility.evidence: MODEL_DERIVED — the capability is novel per moat map, but no in vivo proof exists

product_utility.what_cerevasc_could_sell: eShunt with retention module — a product line extension of the existing eShunt platform
product_utility.evidence: MODEL_SUPPORTED — requires CereVasc's existing eShunt manufacturing and regulatory infrastructure

platform_utility.multiple_therapeutics: YES — size-selective membrane is therapeutic-agnostic; any therapeutic above MWCO is retained
platform_utility.evidence: MODEL_SUPPORTED — membrane physics supports multiple therapeutics, but each requires clinical validation

ip_utility.blocks_competitors: PARTIAL — blocks direct endovascular CSF-venous retention; does not block VP shunt (DA3) or alternative mechanisms (DA2, DA6, DA7) without continuation claims
ip_utility.evidence: UNRESOLVED — 103 status uncertain; moat strength depends on continuation claims (Task 9)

economic_utility.why_acquire_vs_build: CereVasc has the eShunt platform, regulatory infrastructure, and clinical relationships. Building from scratch would take a competitor 4+ years. Acquisition is faster.
economic_utility.evidence: MODEL_SUPPORTED — assumes CereVasc's existing infrastructure; not verified
